title: Development and Validation of Highly Accelerated 4D Flow MRI for Quantitative Assessment of Cardiovascular Haemodynamics at 1.5T, 3T and 7T
summary:
The heart constantly adapts its pumping capacity to changing demands. In the FLOWER study, we are investigating how this adaptation can be measured using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to assess blood flow. In the long term, this is expected to lead to a new metric for cardiac stress testing. In the future, it could help distinguish between healthy circulatory adaptation and that impaired by disease.

To this end, we are developing and testing an accelerated 4D-Flow MRI. This method provides a three-dimensional, time-series representation of blood flow in the heart and major vessels. Our goal is to obtain continuous imaging before, during, and after a targeted change in circulatory conditions. The data are then analyzed in such a way that even brief changes in blood flow can be detected, if possible. If this proves insufficiently reliable, we use a rapid two-dimensional flow measurement to determine appropriate time points for targeted, brief 4D flow imaging.

Healthy adults are participating in the study. Measurements are taken at rest, as well as during passive leg elevation, while squeezing a hand grip strengthener, and, if applicable, during active leg exercise against an adjustable resistance. We compare the accelerated measurement with established methods and assess how accurately and reproducibly it captures blood flow and its changes.

Development and testing are conducted using research equipment and clinical 3T MRI and 1.5T MRI scanners. Supplementary examinations using a 7T MRI scanner are planned as an option. Depending on the study phase, participants undergo different examinations; not all participants go through every phase. Contrast agents and ionizing radiation are not used.

The results are intended to lay the groundwork for future studies in people with cardiovascular diseases or altered circulatory conditions, such as following the implantation of a liver shunt (TIPS). Patients with these conditions are not yet being studied in this trial.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥18 years
Informed written consent
Capacity to give consent and sufficient understanding of the study protocol
No known relevant cardiovascular, pulmonary, or neurological disease
Eligibility for an MRI scan
Ability to perform the prescribed breathing, preload, and exercise maneuvers
Willingness to participate in the scheduled work packages and MRI appointments
Exclusion criteria:
General MRI contraindications, particularly implants or metallic foreign bodies that are not MR-safe
Pregnancy or pregnancy that has not been reliably ruled out
Severe claustrophobia or inability to lie still and flat
Known structural heart disease, significant cardiac arrhythmia, or heart failure
Uncontrolled hypertension or abnormal circulatory parameters on the day of the examination
Acute illness, fever, or impaired general condition
Use of hemodynamically relevant medications, provided these could significantly influence the study measurements
Body dimensions that do not permit a safe examination in the respective MRI system
Inability to give informed consent or withdrawal of consent
Additional exclusion criteria for WP3
Relevant orthopedic, neuromuscular, or vascular diseases of the upper or lower extremities
Pain or restricted movement that prevents a handgrip test, passive leg raise, or active leg loading
Newly occurring symptoms, abnormal blood pressure response, or arrhythmia during a stress maneuver
Additional exclusion criteria for 7 T
Implants or foreign materials not expressly approved for 7 T
Other non-compliance with local 7 T safety guidelines
Incompatibility with the spatial or acoustic conditions of the 7 T system
